summary: Michel Jacq-Hergoualc'h worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied under Jean Boisselier in 1988 and served as a professor at Sorbonne Nouvelle University from circa 1989 to 2003.

Linguist Michel Lejeune studied at the École Normale Supérieure (~1926-1929) and under Antoine Meillet (~1926-1930). He held posts at the University of Poitiers (~1937-1947), École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1947-1977), and the University of Paris (~1951-1977).

Michel Mohr is a scholar of Buddhist, religious, and Japanese studies who completed his Ph.D. at the University of Geneva and studied under Seizan Yanagida. His posts include the University of Geneva, Hanazono University, and the University of Hawaiʻi.

Michel Soymié specialized in Sinology and Buddhist studies, graduating from INALCO by 1952. He held posts at CNRS, the Maison Franco-Japonaise, the École Française d'Extrême-Orient, the Société Asiatique, and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1966-1992).

Strickmann worked in Sinology, Buddhist, and religious studies. He studied at EPHE and Paris Diderot, learning under Hulsewé, Zürcher, Vos, Kaltenmark, Stein, Vandermeersch, Schipper, and Okumura. He held posts at UC Berkeley, the University of Bordeaux, and IAS Berlin.

Michela Clemente works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Elena De Rossi Filibeck and Hildegard Diemberger (2013-2015), and she served as a Marie Sklodowska Curie Fellow at the University of Cambridge.

Michele Kerbaker was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Turin (~1853-1857) and under Giacomo Lignana and Mario Vallauri. He taught Sanskrit at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (1870) and was a professor at Federico II (~1872-1910).
Michele Martin is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Yale University and held a post at National Taiwan University.

Michelle C. Wang works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history/archaeology. She completed her doctoral studies under Eugene Y. Wang and served as an assistant professor of art and art history at Georgetown University (~2012-2018).

Michelle Spuler is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD from the University of Queensland (~1996-2000). She held teaching posts at Colorado College and Victoria University of Wellington (~2001-2004).
Michiel de Vaan specializes in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Alexander Lubotsky (~1998-2002) and held a post at Leiden University from circa 2003 to 2014.

Michihiko Komine is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University (~1964-1974). He held posts at Taisho University as an assistant (~1974-1980) and professor (~1993-2016), and led the Japanese Association for Esoteric Buddhist Studies in 2015.

Michihiko Yajima is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He was a graduate student (attested 1981) and held a post (attested 1992) at the University of Tokyo, later serving as a professor at Tsurumi University (attested 2003-2008).

Michihiro Ikeda is a scholar in Buddhist studies. His career posts include lecturer roles at Setagaya Gakuen (attested 1996) and Komazawa Junior College (attested 2005), as well as librarian at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2005).

Michiko Yusa works in religious studies, philosophy, and Japanology. She earned her PhD at the University of California, Santa Barbara, under Raimon Panikkar, and became a professor of foreign languages at Western Washington University circa 1983.

Michio Kamikawa specializes in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Ritsumeikan University from circa 1979 to 1988 and held a post at Aichi Prefectural University around 1996.

Michio Yano is an Indologist and historian who earned degrees at Kyoto University, studying under Kiyoshi Yabuuchi, and at Brown University under David Pingree. He served as a professor in the Faculty of Cultural Studies at Kyoto Sangyo University (1973-2015).

Michitoshi Barada works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Jien Abe and J. R. Joshi, including at Savitribai Phule Pune University in 1997, and held posts at Otani University, the Eastern Institute, and the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.
Michiya Ito was a graduate student at Tohoku University (attested 1986-1990) and later held an academic post there (attested 2001-2004).
Michiyo Demoto is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at Kyoto University and is attested in a post at the University of Marburg in 2024.
